findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand-sinks are supplied with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A banana stored in the cooler near the tripe sink was observed in a decaying condition. The banana had turned completely black, losing its natural yellow color. Shown to PIC and the banana was discarded. Ensure that food intended for public consumption is always in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility was observed using a plastic grocery bag to store cut sweet potatoes in a prep cooler. Although the sweet potatoes a fried before being served, the practice of storing food items in plastic grocery bags isn’t ideal. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. The potatoes were transferred to an appropriate container to correct the violation. Ensure that foods are stored in food grade products and never in plastic bags.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of both fryers were observed with a significant amount of dried grease debris. PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles manually in the triple sink. Discussed contacting an outside company to service the duct work of the overhead hood system. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink in back does not have disposable towels. Towels were provided to the hand sink. Provide a holder for towels at the hand sink in the back and maintain it stocked with hand towels. The violation is considered corrected at this time. Inspector suggests providing a more permanent place for towels so that a supply remains at the hand sink.

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Inspector observed a container of milk base in the prep cooler reach in section which is dated 10/24/24. This quart of liquid was discarded at time of inspection. Make sure to provide date mark that does not wipe off. Hot dogs and cheese in containers on the top of large prep table in back have labels that allow the date to wipe off. The date is barely visible. Ensure that the date is visible.

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
